source_method: Read-only inspection of installed ELF strings (including embedded user guide and source renderer paths), then full public official source renderer/input-handler audit. The installed build commit is not in the public repository history; public source is a synced monorepo snapshot, so exact installed-source equality is not claimed.
fixture_method: Synthetic native frames built from audited public renderer shapes and input handlers, cross-checked against installed embedded string labels. Fixtures are not native-binary captured screenshots or proof of exact binary/source identity.
coverage_statement: All discovered menu families are inventoried. Supported means the complete stated native renderer shape is projected; remaining families stay in PTY with explicit reasons. This is not a claim of 100% installed-binary menu coverage.
keybinding_caveat: Question/permission/picker keys are literal handlers in the audited source. Custom action bindings, optional feature gates and arbitrary input schemas are not inferred. Native fields with existing drafts remain in PTY except the one-line command-pattern editor, whose Ctrl-U clear() is source-proven.

categories.native_fallback_reason: Authentication launch and token/browser/device/command login modes are left in the native terminal. Never expose credential text inputs, account tokens, browser cookies or session secrets.

Consent/account/team-managed/ZDR notices use separate welcome banners and link actions, not the audited question or picker card. The installed feature-gate rendering and full disclosure must be verified before projection.

Browse/filter/group rows use custom tables, mixed inline toggles and state-dependent editors; arbitrary fields may contain sensitive values. Enum, integer and reset subdialogs are supported separately.
Arbitrary schema fields, validation errors, focus and secret classification are unavailable in screen-only form projection; preserve native fields and explicit Accept/Decline.
URL consent/waiting modes have scrolling URL bodies, invalid/credential-bearing targets and separate action focus. A clipped URL or spoofing warning must never become an approval card.
Full plan disclosure and existing comment drafts live in a separately scrollable preview; cannot infer complete plan from a clipped prompt.
Rewind uses an OverlayList and phase-specific full-screen flow; dedicated tail-marker recognition is still required. Current partial/clipped turn previews stay native.
Session picker contains expandable history cards and asynchronously loaded lanes; complete native row boundaries and delete disclosure are not represented by generic model-choice rows.
Tabbed hierarchical entries expose enable/disable, install/uninstall, source editors, managed connectors, authentication and independent focus; retain native flow.
Hierarchical folds and selected group semantics differ from question checkbox rows; native import confirmation requires its own source-specific projection.
Persona detail field editors, bundled read-only records and external editor actions require separate value/secret rules.
Feedback reports contain multiline drafts, images, remote-unknown recovery states, saved draft deletion and sensitive trace-consent choices. Preserve native review flow.
Dashboard is a multi-pane independent app with agent/session focus, pinned/reordered rows and confirmation timers; no ordinary composer menu fabricated.
Task/workflow/goal panes select running entities and own transport actions; native focus is distinct from composer questions.
Read-only or hierarchical navigators use scrolling documents, key capture and independent value editors. No model or approval question is implied.
Current label may be clipped and source clearing behavior has not been established for this dialog; retain native label editing.
Installed binary embeds announcement/update UI but no complete ordinary choose/update dialog was established. Informational update progress is not a question.
Interactive search/turn jump/editor suggestions have state-dependent keys and text drafts; these are native navigation/editor surfaces.
